P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false

1. Scope and notation


Work on the unchanged positive primitive Stage37 physical endpoint source with R<=B and the current primary large-kernel condition
  sf(G0)>T0,  T0:=B^(1/3-delta),
where G0=gcd(eR,xy) and we take 0<delta<1/3 as the fixed primary-gate margin.


Retain the 229BY hard13 minimum k13, the 229CC six pairwise-coprime odd squarefree buckets
  eta, tau, J, M_U, M_V, M_z,
with eta=rad(Q) in the current notation firewall, and
  K_cross=eta*tau*J*M_U*M_V*M_z=rad_odd(Omega*Pi).
Retain 229CW/229CX
  N_an=S^2-6d^2>0,
and the three 229BL outer pair products
  (R-U)(R-V), (R-z)(R-V), (R-z)(R-U).


2. Auxiliary thresholds are independent of the primary gate threshold


The previous cards proved uniform low-value bounds for every 1<=Z<=B:
  #{k13<=Z} << Z B^o(1)                         by 229BY,
  #{K_cross<=Z} << Z B^o(1)                     by 229CC,
  #{N_an<=Z} << (1+Z) B^o(1)                    by 229CW/229CX,
and the union of the three 229BL small-pair-product sectors at cutoff Z is
  << Z^(1+o(1)).


These are auxiliary fixed-fiber/scoped bounds. Their cutoff does not have to equal T0.


Hence for every fixed 0<epsilon<1/3, putting
  Z_epsilon:=B^(1/3-epsilon),
the union of all four low-auxiliary events above is
  O(B^(1/3-epsilon+o(1)))=o(B^(1/3)).


In particular, once the primary gate supplies a fixed delta>0, one may canonically choose
  epsilon=delta/2,
  Z:=B^(1/3-delta/2),
which is strictly larger than T0 for B>1.


RESULT_229CZ_AUXILIARY_CUTOFF_DECOUPLES_FROM_PRIMARY_GATE=PROVED_SCOPED.


3. Two-scale strengthened residual


Up to o(B^(1/3)) endpoints, the unchanged primary-gate source may therefore be restricted simultaneously to


  sf(G0)>B^(1/3-delta),


  k13>Z,
  K_cross>Z,
  N_an>Z,


and
  (R-U)(R-V)>Z,
  (R-z)(R-V)>Z,
  (R-z)(R-U)>Z,


with
  Z=B^(1/3-delta/2).


Call this the TWO_SCALE_HARD14 residual: “14” records the 13 retained k13 radical tests plus the single joint-union radical K_cross. N_an and the three pair products are retained geometric/anisotropy hardening conditions and are not counted as additional radical labels.


No selector, positivity, primitivity, physical-height, or square condition is removed.


RESULT_229CZ_TWO_SCALE_HARD14_REDUCTION=PROVED_SCOPED.
RESULT_229CZ_KCROSS_CAN_BE_FORCED_ABOVE_NEAR_ONE_THIRD_AT_O_B_ONE_THIRD_COST=PROVED_SCOPED.


4. Delta-decoupled six-bucket amplification


The deterministic 229CA/229CC hard13 derivation depends only on the common lower threshold imposed on the hard10/pair-sum-radical conditions. On TWO_SCALE_HARD14 those conditions hold at Z, not merely at T0.


Therefore the 229CC balanced choice alpha=beta=gamma=1/5 can be rerun verbatim with Z in place of T0. Every endpoint in TWO_SCALE_HARD14 satisfies


  eta>Z^(1/5)
  OR tau>Z^(1/5)
  OR J>Z^(1/5)
  OR max(M_U,M_V,M_z)>2^(-3/2) Z^(1/5).


Since Z=B^(1/3-delta/2),
  Z^(1/5)=B^(1/15-delta/10).


The previous same-delta threshold was
  T0^(1/5)=B^(1/15-delta/5).


Thus the six-bucket forced scale is strictly strengthened while the primary G0 gate is unchanged.


RESULT_229CZ_SIX_BUCKET_THRESHOLD_RAISED_FROM_T0_ONE_FIFTH_TO_Z_ONE_FIFTH=PROVED_EXACT_ON_THE_SCOPED_RESIDUAL.


More generally, for any fixed 0<epsilon<delta one may take Z_epsilon=B^(1/3-epsilon), obtaining bucket scale B^(1/15-epsilon/5), arbitrarily close to B^(1/15) at fixed positive epsilon.


5. What this does and does not solve


This is a genuine source hardening and theorem-interface improvement, not a global count.


The current blocker remains: none of the large eta, tau, J, or M_i branches has a selector-aware occupied-support estimate at the required one-third endpoint budget. Likewise K_cross>Z is a strong one-scalar joint-support condition with B^o(1) fixed-k fibers, but fixed fibers plus a lower radical bound do not imply an occupied-tail estimate.


Do not:
- promote the scoped o(B^(1/3)) removals to global counting credit;
- multiply the six bucket densities;
- treat K_cross as independent of its six factors;
- change the primary G0 threshold from B^(1/3-delta);
- revive 229BY Section 5's retracted radical triangle;
- infer endpoint sparsity from a large support value without a realized-image theorem.


6. Updated research interface

TWO_SCALE_HARD14_WITH_PRIMARY_G0_T0_AND_AUXILIARY_Z_NEAR_ONE_THIRD / PARALLEL_WHOLE_G0_AND_229CC_SIX_BUCKET_OCCUPANCY / 229CT_PRIMARY_FOR_J_ONLY.

NO_SELECTOR_AWARE_OR_OCCUPIED_SUPPORT_SAVING_FOR_THE_229CC_SIX_BUCKET_COVER_ON_THE_TWO_SCALE_HARD14_EXACT_PHYSICAL_SOURCE.

(A) whole-source sf(G0)>T0 via 229AR or another selector-aware occupied-support theorem;
(B) the 229CC six-bucket cover at the strengthened cutoff Z^(1/5), with 229CT as J-only primary;
(C) a direct realized occupied-tail theorem for K_cross>Z using the existing B^o fixed-k fiber;
(D) 229BF only if both outer-count and reciprocal-height weighted mass are saved, or the inner theorem is strengthened.
Keep 229CX anisotropy and 229BL pair-product reductions at the synchronized Z cutoff. External theorem adapters remain conditional on proved host hypotheses.

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CY — quantitative route audit
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA=Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CX
OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY=M3-T11-229
PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
M3-T11-230=NOT_ISSUED


RESULT_229CY_AUDIT_SUMMARY: The 229BF outer-triple count has TWO quantitatively insufficient terms, not only a one-per-outer floor. For each primitive outer triple of height H, 229BF gives N_outer(B,T) <= B^o(1)*(1+B/(H*T)). Summing over all primitive outer Pythagorean triples with H<=B is bounded only by B^o(1)*(B+B*log(2B)/T). At T=B^(1/3-delta), even the second term scales as B^(2/3+delta+o(1)), above the required B^(1/3). These are bounds from the method, NOT lower bounds for actual physical endpoints.


2. Why unrestricted outer summation has these sizes.
Each primitive outer triple is parametrized by coprime opposite-parity integers m>n>0 with H=m*m+n*n (up to 2 leg orders). There are O(B) choices with H<=B. In dyadic annuli 2^j<=H<2^(j+1), there are O(2^j) integer pairs each weighted O(2^(-j)), giving a total reciprocal-height mass O(log B). Hence the BF sum is the bound already displayed. No bound on selector-qualified outer support with a power saving was proved.


3. 229AR overlap audit.
229AR states W_minus=UV-eR=2^epsilon*G_star*r_minus^2 and sf_odd(W_minus)=sf_odd(G_star), where G_star=gcd(eR,xy). The 229BF bound already imposes K_star=sf(G_star)>T on the SAME physical source. Thus the W_minus radical condition is a deterministic restatement of that event. Combining the two facts does not create an additional independent density factor or sharper inner fibre bound.
RESULT_229CY_229AR_PLUS_229BF_NO_NEW_MULTIPLICATIVE_SAVING=METHOD_FIREWALL.


4. Required alternative quantitative theorem.
For dyadic H~Y, let A_Y(B) be an explicitly specified OUTER-ONLY necessary-condition superset of possible physical outer triples, not a circular set defined by the unknown endpoints themselves. From 229BF, it would be sufficient for some fixed rho>0 to prove
SUM_Y #A_Y(B)*(1+B/(Y*T)) << B^(1/3-rho),
keeping all selectors and bounded reconstruction. This demands both sum #A_Y << B^(1/3-rho) and (B/T)*sum(#A_Y/Y) << B^(1/3-rho), or else an improved inner count replacing 229BF. None is presently available.


Proof of outer sums: primitive Pythagorean triples have H=m^2+n^2 for coprime opposite-parity m>n>0, up to two orientations. The disk m^2+n^2<=B contains O(B) integer pairs. The dyadic annulus 2^j<=H<2^(j+1) has O(2^j) pairs, each with 1/H=O(2^(-j)), so sum_{outer} 1/H=O(log(2B)). No selector-conditioned improvement for the outer sums has yet been established.


229AR vs 229BF: Wminus=UV-eR equals 2^epsilon times Gstar times a square, with Gstar=gcd(eR,xy). Its odd squarefree kernel is the same as Gstar's. Since 229BF already imposes large sf(Gstar), 229AR restates that same arithmetic condition. No independent numerical improvement follows from placing the two formulas together.


DECISION_229CY: Replace only the research priority of 229CX. Keep the near-isotropy small-sector result and all existing theorems. The 229AR and 229BF routes remain available but are not the exclusive main direction. In parallel, examine the full radical-kernel counting target, the six-bucket cover with 229CT for its J branch, and external theorems only when their hypotheses are met. No overall counting improvement is claimed. Existing authority, gate, credit and closure remain unchanged. Independent hostile audit not run.


NEXT_RESEARCH_INPUT: On the exact positive primitive Stage37 hard13 physical source with R<=B and sf(gcd(eR,xy))>B^(1/3-delta), seek selector-aware counting savings. Maintain the 229CC six-bucket union and 229CT J-only primary. For any renewed 229BF outer-slice proposal, bound both the number of admissible outer triples and their reciprocal-height mass; removing only the per-outer floor is insufficient. Retain the 229CW/229CX low-anisotropy disposal and the 229BL small-gap-product disposal. GitHub openai/math adapter bridges remain unproved. CARD_DOC_ID=1xNhyyfOLkTzR-GGqBaF2V4s0PtDkDsdf0sCPlFz0UZU. NEXT_NEW_CHAT_CAN_RESUME_FROM_DRIVE_ONLY=true.

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CX — near-isotropy sector disposal and openai/math route audit
CARD_DOC_ID=1-hZMR8ANURcMrGwulAVjTkLAxUleHCOq1I7hcL60CI8
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA=Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CW
STATUS: POST_229CW_NEW_SCOPED_COUNT / NEAR_EQUAL_OUTER_GAP_O_M3_DISPOSAL / POST_229CT_229AR_229BF_ROUTE_PRIORITY_AUDIT / GITHUB_OPENAI_MATH_ADAPTER_RECHECK / NO_GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT / NO_REOPEN
OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY=M3-T11-229; LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION=M3-T11-228; M3-T11-230 NOT_ISSUED.
PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN; GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0; P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false.
RESEARCH_PRODUCTION_STATUS=HOLD_PENDING_SELECTOR_AWARE_OR_SUPPORT_LEVEL_THEOREM_INPUT.
INDEPENDENT_HOSTILE_AUDIT_229CX=NOT_RUN. This is a scoped in-session route audit, NOT a separate-chat certification.


1. Exact source


Work throughout on Stage37 exact positive primitive hard13 physical endpoints S_B^hard13(delta), R<=B, including all retained space/face square selectors.
A=R-U, Bv=R-V, C=R-z, S=A+Bv+C=R-2d>0, ABv+AC+BvC=2d^2.
Recall 229CW exact anisotropy scalar
N_an=S^2-6d^2=(Y^2+3X^2)/4, X=A-Bv, Y=A+Bv-2C,
with N_an a positive integer N_an<B^2 and UNIFORM fixed-value physical fiber
#{P:R<=B,N_an(P)=n}=B^o(1) for each 1<=n<B^2.
This prior fixed-value result follows by real Q(sqrt6) norm/Pell ideal generators O(tau(n)^O(1) log B) and Eisenstein imaginary norm representations O(tau(n)), with at most one physical endpoint per resulting gap triple. It is NOT a theorem counting all occupied n.


2. New exact symmetric anisotropy and genuinely counted small sector


An elementary rearrangement of the exact cone yields:
(A-Bv)^2+(Bv-C)^2+(C-A)^2
=2[(A^2+Bv^2+C^2)-(ABv+AC+BvC)]
=2[(S^2-4d^2)-2d^2]
=2N_an.                                                        (CX.1)
Thus
N_an=(1/2)*SUM_over_three_unordered_gap_pairs(diff^2).          (CX.2)
This identifies 229CW's double-norm receiver as the EXACT squared distance to the diagonal A=Bv=C in the outer-gap plane.


For H>=1 define E_an(B,H):={actual Stage37 positive primitive physical endpoints P:R(P)<=B, 1<=N_an(P)<=H}. With the uniform fixed-n fiber from 229CW,
#E_an(B,H) <= sum_{1<=n<=min(H,B^2)} B^o(1)
              <= (1+H) B^o(1).                                (CX.3)
Uniformly for any fixed epsilon>0, choose H=B^(1/3-epsilon). Then
#E_an(B,B^(1/3-epsilon))
<< B^(1/3-epsilon+o(1)) = o(B^(1/3)).                        (CX.4)
The same bound holds for its intersection with the hard13 large-sf(G0)>T source and any other selectors. No independent population is introduced.


Let D>=0 and D_max=max(|A-Bv|,|Bv-C|,|C-A|). By (CX.2), N_an<=3D^2/2 whenever D_max<=D, so
#{P:R<=B,D_max(P)<=D} << (1+D^2) B^o(1).                    (CX.5)
Thus D=B^(1/6-epsilon) (epsilon>0 fixed, exponent positive) gives a true o(B^(1/3)) near-equal-gap sector, with its O(B^(1/3-2epsilon+o(1))) bound.


On the complementary hard remainder one may now impose
N_an > B^(1/3-epsilon), hence
max(|A-Bv|,|Bv-C|,|C-A|)
   > sqrt(2/3)*B^(1/6-epsilon/2),                            (CX.6)
in addition to 229BL's three already-large outer-pair products and the retained hard13 selector masks, at scoped o(B^(1/3)) cost.


RESULT_229CX_NEAR_ISOTROPY_SECTOR_HAS_H_B_O_COUNT=PROVED_SCOPED.
RESULT_229CX_NEAR_EQUAL_OUTER_GAP_SECTOR_IS_O_B_ONE_THIRD=PROVED_SCOPED.
RESULT_229CX_HARD_REMAINDER_HAS_EXPLICIT_GAP_ANISOTROPY_LOWER_BOUND=PROVED_SCOPED.
This is a legitimate additional sector disposal. GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT remains 0 because the complementary anisotropic population is still uncounted.


3. Hostile limits of the double-norm idea


The facts "N_an is a norm from Q(sqrt6)" and "N_an is an Eisenstein norm" refer to one and the same scalar, not two independent rare sieve events. The Eisenstein local support rule (all p==2 mod3 inert primes have even n-valuation) and the q=gcd(R,S)=gcd(R,d) square-divisor / p==1 mod12 facts do not force q large: q can equal 1. Neither fact currently estimates the number of n>B^(1/3-epsilon) realized by hard13 physical endpoints.


To expose the ambient-model gap, consider the positive OUTER-CONE family
A=Bv=2k, C=k, d=2k, S=5k, R=9k (k>=1).
It satisfies ABv+AC+BvC=8k^2=2d^2 and N_an=S^2-6d^2=k^2. There is one such represented scalar for every k. The derived formal diagonals U=V=7k,z=8k give e^2=R^2-z^2=17k^2, not a physical square for nonzero k. This family is not primitive nor is it an Euler/perfect cuboid source; it shows that the CONE and dual norm identity ALONE do not imply enough occupied-N sparsity. Any global theorem must use the omitted physical selectors. Do not promote this cone family to a counterexample to a theorem on exact hard13.


RESULT_229CX_DOUBLE_NORM_ONLY_HAS_NO_PROVED_GLOBAL_OCCUPANCY_SAVING=METHOD_FIREWALL.


4. Verified openai/math snapshot and host-gate audit (read-only)


Public source: https://github.com/openai/math
GitHub current default=main. GitHub commits query on 2026-10-08 JST returned ONE commit:
SHA=adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a
MESSAGE=Initial commit, created_at=2026-10-06T21:58:50Z.
Current relevant source files were fetched from this repository (the same SHA cited in existing Stage37 cards 229CD/229CE):
A. https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/lean/OAI/NumberTheory/EgyptianFractions/RoughModulusCollision.lean
   theorem moduli_rpow_energy_card_le; requires a SINGLE COMMON finite pool A across all q, a quantitative high collision energy for EVERY q, and restricted off-diagonal divisor multiplicity. Stage37 229CB offers only one unary root-line condition on each q-DEPENDENT physical endpoint fiber. Existing 229CE TAU_FIXED_BASE_COLLISION_AMPLIFICATION is still missing. Do not multiply per-q local root data into a common-pool collision theorem.
B. https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/lean/OAI/NumberTheory/Ostmann/QuadraticSieveLargeGcd.lean
   theorem weighted_large_gcd_removal controls a JACOBI CHARACTER ENERGY for odd squarefree columns via small-gcd strata plus shorter quotient norm. Stage37 229CT full-J marked (H_J,C_J) is a SPARSE matched physical incidence and has no proven energy lower bound/factorable Cartesian weight transfer; existing 229CE J_SPARSE_MATCHED_INCIDENCE_BILINEARIZATION remains missing.
C. https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/lean/OAI/NumberTheory/Ostmann/Quadratic/QuadraticKernelCount.lean
   theorem quadratic_biased_kernel_count requires PublishedQuadraticLargeSieve input AND a uniform positive common-prime quadraticPrimeMean bias on the counted kernels. The Stage37 J/tau/M_i root/gcd marks do not supply such a global shared bias.
D. https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/lean/OAI/NumberTheory/Ostmann/Characters/AffineKernelCount.lean
   eventual_affine_kernel_count requires a genuine affine-value kernel host and the same common-prime bias + scale hypotheses. W_-=UV-eR has the exact squarefree kernel of G0 by 229AR, but is a BILINEAR value in endpoint variables and is not currently shown to be a bounded-fiber affine family with the required common center/bias. Merely rewriting 229AR into one scalar does not discharge this theorem's hypotheses.
The README explicitly cautions not all manuscripts are formalized and unformalized statements can have issues; do not promote theorem titles/repository existence to a Stage37 unconditional counting result.


RESULT_229CX_OPENAI_MATH_COMMIT_UNCHANGED_FROM_229CD_CE=VERIFIED_AT_CHECK_TIME.
RESULT_229CX_DIRECT_OPENAI_MATH_ONE_THIRD_TRANSFER=NOT_ESTABLISHED_HOST_GAPS_REMAIN.
No GitHub files were modified.


5. Route selection audit and concrete priority


Decision: KEEP Stage37 M3-T11-229 authority/HOLD/GATE OPEN and DO NOT replace 229CT as the PRIMARY FULL-J SUBBRANCH receiver. But CHANGE immediate RESEARCH EMPHASIS away from generating repeated exact gcd/norm encodings with no global counting input.


Priority 0: apply proved 229CX near-isotropy disposal and retained 229BL small-pair-product disposal at total o(B^(1/3)) cost; record BOTH inequalities on the SAME remaining hard13 source:
- N_an>B^(1/3-epsilon)
- (R-U)(R-V), (R-z)(R-V), (R-z)(R-U)>B^(1/3-eta), with fixed epsilon,eta>0.
This is localization, not proof that all six branches are closed.


Priority 1: attack the WHOLE preferred large-kernel source directly, rather than only one of 229CC's six buckets. The strongest direct candidate remains 229AR
W_-:=UV-eR>0, sf_odd(W_-)=sf_odd(G0), W_-<B^2,
which keeps the full threshold T/2. Pair with 229BF's only EXISTING quantitative fixed-outer theorem
N_outer(B,T)<<B^o(1)(1+B/(HT)).
Precisely isolate its residual "one per outer" floor. Seek a selector-aware bound for OCCUPIED outer parameters or strong fiber cancellation that overcomes that floor on the entire anisotropic hard remainder. Neither 229AR nor 229BF currently closes it.
Priority 2: if direct whole-source bridge fails, resume 229CT full-J triangle occupation on the J large bucket while retaining 229CP R/P/B/S states, 229CS/CU B-state and 229CV geometric mark. However J alone closes only one branch of the six-bucket cover; it cannot be globally promoted without eta, tau, M_i branch controls.
Priority 3: openai/math modules are CONDITIONAL adapters only: explicitly prove ONE missing common-pool tau collision, sparse-incidence Jacobi energy, or affine-kernel shared-bias bridge before invoking published external machinery. No new bridge was found on the unchanged source.
Do not pursue 229CW's q or Eisenstein local congruences as an independent large-prime sieve. Keep the new 229CX near-isotropy theorem in the saved arsenal.


NEXT_THEOREM_CONTRACT:
On exact S_B^hard13(delta) with R<=B, sf(G0)>B^(1/3-delta), and after the two charged-once scoped exclusions, either
(i) prove a quantitative occupied-outer count/weighted distribution overcoming the 229BF one-per-outer floor for 229AR W_- source, or
(ii) prove a selector-aware occupied-support theorem for K_* via 229AR directly, or
(iii) exhibit full host verification for one openai/math adapter, not merely an algebraic analogy.
Any valid global count needs o(B^(1/3)); preserve original exact selectors, truncation, physical endpoint measure, and all prior retraction/firewalls.

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CW — positive anisotropy double norm and Eisenstein gcd conductor
CARD_DOC_ID=1fDqUi04pmUDGvYQxcX7HJ1nnhuBMZ77jeLE-WI0VEG8

A=R-U, Bv=R-V, C=R-z; S=A+Bv+C=R-2d, d>0.
By 229BU/229CB, A Bv + A C + Bv C=2d^2; S and R are odd (229BX).
Let Omega=A Bv C, s=A+Bv, t=A+C, u=Bv+C, Pi=s t u.
Retain 229CF/CG: lambda_U=gcd(A,S), lambda_V=gcd(Bv,S), lambda_z=gcd(C,S) are odd pairwise coprime; L_J=lambda_U lambda_V lambda_z=gcd(Omega,S)=gcd(Pi,S), J=rad(L_J), and gcd(L_J,d)=1.
Retain all existing 229CC six buckets, 229CT full-J norm-S gcd primary, 229CV geometric height adapter and 229BY Sections2-4; 229BY Section5 radical triangle remains retracted by 229BZ.


2. New quadratic-height positive anisotropy receiver


Define
N_an := S^2 - 6d^2.                                          (CW.1)
Let X=A-Bv and Y=A+Bv-2C=S-3C.
The cone identity sum(A_i^2)=S^2-4d^2 gives
Y^2 + 3X^2
 = 6(A^2+Bv^2+C^2)-2S^2
 = 4(S^2-6d^2)
 = 4 N_an.                                                     (CW.2)
Since X and Y have the same parity, alpha=(Y+X sqrt(-3))/2 is an algebraic integer of the Eisenstein ring Z[(1+sqrt(-3))/2], with
Norm_{Q(sqrt(-3))/Q}(alpha)=N_an.                              (CW.3)
N_an>=0. Equality would give X=Y=0, hence A=Bv=C, U=V=z and e=x=y; then U^2=2e^2, impossible for positive integers. Therefore actual physical endpoints satisfy
0<N_an<S^2<R^2<=B^2.                                        (CW.4)
On the other hand
N_an=Norm_{Q(sqrt(6))/Q}(S+d sqrt(6))                        (CW.5)
is simultaneously a real quadratic norm.
RESULT_229CW_POSITIVE_QUADRATIC_HEIGHT_DOUBLE_NORM_ANISOTROPY_SCALAR=PROVED_EXACT.
The two norm descriptions are the SAME scalar of ONE physical endpoint. They are not independent sieve factors.


3. Uniform B^o(1) fixed-N physical fiber


Fix n=N_an>0, n<B^2.
Step A (real norm): S^2-6d^2=n with 0<S<R<=B and 0<d<B. In the fixed real quadratic field Q(sqrt(6)), each algebraic integer S+d sqrt(6) of norm n generates an integral ideal of norm n. There are at most tau(n)^O(1) such ideals (prime-ideal factorization in a fixed degree-2 field); generators of one ideal differ by units. The norm-positive real units are generated up to sign by a fixed fundamental unit (5+2sqrt(6)); restricting both positive embeddings and 0<S,d<B leaves O(1+log B) unit translates. Therefore uniformly
# {(S,d): S^2-6d^2=n, 0<S,d<B} << tau(n)^O(1)(1+log B) = B^o(1).  (CW.6)
No class-number-one assumption is needed for this upper bound: count only principal ideals among all norm-n ideals.


Step B (imaginary norm): for each fixed (S,d), (CW.2) gives Y^2+3X^2=4n with Y==X mod 2. Since Z[(1+sqrt(-3))/2] is the Eisenstein UFD, the number of algebraic integers alpha of norm n is <=6 tau(n), so there are B^o(1) possible ordered (X,Y).
The gaps are uniquely recovered from
C=(S-Y)/3,
A=(2S+Y+3X)/6,
Bv=(2S+Y-3X)/6.                                        (CW.7)
Nonintegral, nonpositive or nonphysical candidates are discarded. Each surviving labelled positive gap triple determines at most one positive physical endpoint by retained 229BU reconstruction (R=S+2d, U=R-A, V=R-Bv, z=R-C, then e,x,y from the squares).
Combining yields uniformly
#{P:R(P)<=B, N_an(P)=n} = B^o(1).                         (CW.8)
RESULT_229CW_FIXED_ANISOTROPY_N_HAS_UNIFORM_SUBPOWER_PHYSICAL_FIBER=PROVED.


The Eisenstein norm also implies N_an is odd, and every p==2 mod 3 has EVEN exponent in N_an; equivalently sf(N_an) is supported only on 3 and primes p==1 mod 3. These are necessary support restrictions, not a fixed-power occupied-value estimate.
RESULT_229CW_ANISOTROPY_N_INERT_PRIMES_HAVE_EVEN_VALUATION=PROVED_EXACT.


4. New full gcd conductor q and exact local splitting


Define
q:=gcd(R,S).                                                (CW.9)
Because R is odd and R=S+2d, exactly
q=gcd(R,S)=gcd(R,d)=gcd(S,d).                              (CW.10)
In particular q is odd and q|R, q|S, q|d, so
q^2|N_an.                                                    (CW.11)
Since gcd(L_J,d)=1, gcd(q,L_J)=1.


For every prime p|q, p|R,S,d. If p divided any gap A,Bv,C, then p would divide its lambda color as well, contradicting gcd(L_J,d)=1. Thus p divides none of A,Bv,C. Since U=R-A, V=R-Bv, z=R-C, p divides none of U,V,z. Then the face equations
y^2=R^2-U^2, x^2=R^2-V^2, e^2=R^2-z^2
show p does not divide e,x,y, and -1 is a quadratic residue modulo p. Therefore p==1 mod4.


Also the exact identities
U+V+z=3R-S,
U^2+V^2+z^2=2R^2
give, modulo q,
U+V+z==0,
U^2+V^2+z^2==0.
As U is a q-unit, t:=V U^(-1) mod q satisfies
t^2+t+1==0 mod q, and z==-(1+t)U mod q.                (CW.12)
Modulo p, p!=3 (as p==1 mod4) and t has multiplicative order exactly 3; hence p==1 mod3. Therefore EVERY prime p|q satisfies
p==1 mod 12,  and q==1 mod 12.                            (CW.13)
The two roots of t^2+t+1 modulo each p^a||q are simple and lift uniquely, giving exactly 2^omega(q) admissible global root classes modulo q.
RESULT_229CW_FULL_R_S_GCD_EISENSTEIN_ROOT_LINE_AND_MOD12_SUPPORT=PROVED_EXACT.


Moreover q is coprime to the full physical outer and pair-sum products: if p|q then p∤A Bv C and, since s=S-C, t=S-Bv, u=S-A, p∤s t u. Thus
gcd(q,Omega Pi)=1.                                         (CW.14)
Also gcd(q,e x y U V z)=1, and gcd(q,G0)=1 for G0=gcd(eR,xy).
In addition for p>3 dividing J, p|S and p∤d (229CF/CG), so
N_an== -6d^2 mod p and p∤N_an.
Thus with J_sharp=J/gcd(J,3),
gcd(N_an,J_sharp)=1.                                        (CW.15)
RESULT_229CW_Q_CONDUCTOR_IS_COPRIME_TO_OMEGA_PI_AND_KERNEL_G0=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229CW_ANISOTROPY_N_SUPPORT_IS_DISJOINT_FROM_THREE_FREE_J=PROVED_EXACT.


This makes q an OPTIONAL orthogonal Eisenstein conductor, not a seventh guaranteed-large six-bucket. q may equal 1.


5. Quantitative ceiling and safe continuation


The fixed-N fiber (CW.8) is a new low-height pushforward: N_an<B^2, each occupied value contains only B^o actual physical endpoints. It does NOT bound the number of actually occupied n. The standard unrestricted ambient count O(B^2) is enormously above the one-third target.


Fix q=m. Since m|R and m|d, there are at most O((B/m)^2) candidate integer pairs (R,d); each fixed pair has B^o physical fiber from Section 3 (its N is determined), so
#{P:R<=B,q(P)=m} << B^o(1)(B/m)^2.                   (CW.16)
This is a charged-once deterministic upper bound, not a claimed independent quadratic-density sieve. Unrestricted summation over q>Q gives only <<B^o B^2/Q, too large to prove o(B^(1/3)) for any admissible Q<=B. The Eisenstein root-class restriction is not independently multiplied into (CW.16).
No large-q, large-N, or mixed J/kernel occupied-support theorem has been established.


New optional theorem interface:
ANISOTROPY_DOUBLE_NORM_OCCUPANCY:
count the ACTUALLY REALIZED N_an values on the exact hard13 source with sf(G0)>T and all retained selectors, using simultaneous real Q(sqrt(6)) and imaginary Q(sqrt(-3)) norm representations and N_an<B^2, fixed-N B^o.

Preserve 229CT full-J primary; 229CV height adapter; 229CU/CS B-state; 229CP R/P/S and eta/tau/M_i/K_cross fallback. Do not treat real and imaginary norms as independent probabilities. ﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CV — sharp physical S/R window and height-adapted full-J split
CARD_DOC_ID=1kVIgFefyOLuhKXtWI0iXarZFzDlZMmT6V-gheZrYghk
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA=Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CU
STATUS: POST_229CU_PHYSICAL_HEIGHT_GEOMETRY / SHARP_CONTINUOUS_S_OVER_R_LOWER_CONSTANT / LARGE_NORM_HEIGHT_EQUIVALENCE / GEOMETRIC_ORIENTATION_FULL_J_TWO_BRANCH_COVER / NO_NEW_GLOBAL_COUNT / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN
OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY=M3-T11-229; LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION=M3-T11-228; M3-T11-230 NOT_ISSUED.
PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN; GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0; P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false; PRODUCTION HOLD.


1. Exact physical source and notation


Work on exactly the positive primitive Stage37 hard13 physical source, all simultaneous face and space square selectors, R<=B:
e^2+x^2=U^2, e^2+y^2=V^2, x^2+y^2=z^2, e^2+x^2+y^2=R^2.
A=R-U, Bv=R-V, C=R-z, S=A+Bv+C=R-2d, d>0.
s=A+Bv, t=A+C, u=Bv+C, H_A=st=A^2+2d^2, H_B=su=Bv^2+2d^2, H_C=tu=C^2+2d^2.
Retain 229CT C_A=gcd(H_A,S)=lambda_Vlambda_z and cyclically; lambda_U=gcd(A,S), lambda_V=gcd(Bv,S), lambda_z=gcd(C,S) are pairwise coprime odd. L_J=lambda_Ulambda_Vlambda_z, J=rad(L_J).
Do not use the retracted 229BY Section5 radical triangle; 229BY Sections2-4 fixed-H_i physical B^o fibers remain retained.


2. Sharp universal physical height window for S


Put weights alpha_e=e^2/R^2, alpha_x=x^2/R^2, alpha_y=y^2/R^2. They are strictly between 0 and 1 and sum to 1.
The exact square relations give
U/R=sqrt(1-alpha_y),
V/R=sqrt(1-alpha_x),
z/R=sqrt(1-alpha_e).
Therefore
S/R=3-[sqrt(1-alpha_e)+sqrt(1-alpha_x)+sqrt(1-alpha_y)].        (CV.1)
Concavity of sqrt and Jensen yield
sum sqrt(1-alpha_i) <= 3sqrt(2/3)=sqrt(6).
The elementary sqrt(1-a)>=1-a inequality gives sum sqrt(1-alpha_i)>2 on the strict positive chamber (strict for 0<a<1).
Hence with c0:=3-sqrt(6)>0,
c0 R <= S < R.                                                   (CV.2)
Equality at the lower bound of the continuous positive-edge cone requires alpha_e=alpha_x=alpha_y=1/3, i.e. e=x=y. This cannot occur in an integer physical Euler brick because e^2+x^2=2e^2 would force U=e sqrt(2) nonintegral. Thus actual positive integer endpoints have STRICT c0 R<S<R. Sharpness is claimed only on the continuous real relaxation, NOT on the actual discrete physical set.
Since R-S=2d,
0<d<(sqrt(6)-2)R/2.                                        (CV.3)
RESULT_229CV_SHARP_REAL_CONE_PHYSICAL_S_OVER_R_WINDOW=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229CV_PHYSICAL_GAP_D_UPPER_CONSTANT=PROVED_EXACT.
This rules out treating S=o(R) as an actual physical subbranch. It does not supply any power saving.


3. A norm receiver whose height is genuinely quadratic in R


Define i_geo by maximizing H_A,H_B,H_C with deterministic tie order A<B<C; put H_geo=H_(i_geo). Since H_A-H_B=A^2-Bv^2, H_A-H_C=A^2-C^2 and cyclically, i_geo is also the index of the largest gap.
Let m=max(A,Bv,C), and let b,c denote the other two gaps, with b+c=S-m and b,c<=m. Then
H_geo=(m+b)(m+c)=m S+b c.                                 (CV.4)
If m>=S/2, then H_geo>=m S>=S^2/2>4S^2/9.
If S/3<=m<=S/2, fixed sum b+c=S-m and constraints b,c<=m imply b c>=m(S-2m) (the product minimum is at the endpoint (b,c)=(m,S-2m) up to exchange). Thus
H_geo>=2m(S-m)>=4S^2/9,
because 2t(1-t) increases for 1/3<=t<=1/2 and equals 4/9 at t=1/3.
Therefore
(4/9) S^2 <= H_geo < S^2 < R^2,                          (CV.5)
with equality in the lower continuous gap cone only when A=Bv=C.
Combining (CV.2),
[4(3-sqrt(6))^2/9] R^2 <= H_geo < R^2.                    (CV.6)
Equivalently
sqrt(H_geo)<R<= 3 sqrt(H_geo)/[2(3-sqrt(6))].             (CV.7)
Actual positive integer points satisfy strict lower inequalities (e=x=y equality impossible).


For each fixed h, the set H_geo=h is contained in the union of the three retained fixed-H_i fibers from 229BY Sections2-4. Therefore its number of whole physical endpoints with R<=B is uniformly B^o(1).
RESULT_229CV_HEIGHT_EQUIVALENT_MAX_NORM_RECEIVER_WITH_B_O_FIXED_FIBER=PROVED.
Unlike an arbitrary J-maximizing norm H_J in 229CT, H_geo is always comparable to R^2. This is a height-normalization improvement, NOT an occupied support bound.


4. Exact height-adapted full-J branch cover


Set C_geo=gcd(H_geo,S), and let lambda_omit be the lambda color attached to the largest gap: if i_geo=A, lambda_omit=lambda_U; if i_geo=B, lambda_omit=lambda_V; if i_geo=C, lambda_omit=lambda_z.
229CT gives C_geo equal to the PRODUCT OF THE OTHER TWO lambda colors, while the three lambda colors are pairwise coprime. Consequently
J=rad(C_geo)*rad(lambda_omit) exactly.                       (CV.8)
For any K>=1 and 0<theta<1,
J>K implies
(a) rad(C_geo)>K^theta,
or
(b) rad(lambda_omit)>K^(1-theta).                            (CV.9)
This is a disjoint decision by testing (a) first; if it fails, (b) holds. On branch (a) the marked norm (H_geo,C_geo) obeys
H_geo>=4 c0^2 R^2/9, H_geo<R^2, C_geo=gcd(H_geo,S)<R,
rad(C_geo)>K^theta,
and the fixed marked-pair physical fiber is B^o(1).
On branch (b), the omitted full lambda divides both its outer gap m and the opposite pair sum S-m, so
lambda_omit | m and lambda_omit | S-m,
lambda_omit <= min(m,S-m) <= S/2,                           (CV.10)
and rad(lambda_omit)>K^(1-theta). This is a genuinely singled-out color, NOT a disposed tail.


In particular at theta=2/3:
J>K => [H_geo comparable to R^2 with rad(gcd(H_geo,S))>K^(2/3)]
OR [the omitted color lambda_omit has rad> K^(1/3)].
This is a height-adapted alternative to 229CT's radical-maximizing orientation. It trades the possible loss of a third-color radical for quadratic physical height normalization; it does not improve the existing K^(2/3) full-J canonical cover.


RESULT_229CV_HEIGHT_ADAPTED_J_SPLIT_WITH_SINGLE_COLOR_FALLBACK=PROVED_EXACT.


5. Scope, quantitative firewall and next input


The two-branch cover (CV.9) does NOT prove that either branch has o(B^(1/3)) endpoints. Its geometric lower bound on H_geo does not create density, and fixed-H B^o fibers do not count occupied values. No independent probability may be attached to the marked gcd, lambda or geometric cone.
The primary same-physical gate remains 229CT J_NORM_S_GCD_TRIANGLE_OCCUPANCY for canonical (H_J,C_J) with rad(C_J)>K^(2/3), sf(G0)>T=B^(1/3-delta).
229CV offers an optional proof adapter: use a theorem that counts the high-height marked image (H_geo,C_geo) on branch (a) AND a selector-aware single-largest-gap lambda occupancy bound on branch (b). Both must meet a fixed-power margin below B^(1/3), and all hard13 physical selectors and the large sf(G0)>T source must remain. The geometric branch may be useful where exact physical height R~sqrt(H_geo) is essential. If a theorem only requires low-height H_J, use 229CT directly.
At the current six-bucket K=T^(1/5), theta=2/3 yields thresholds T^(2/15) and T^(1/15), but NO numerical endpoint saving is proved.
Do not use 229BY Section5; do not treat the two branches as statistically independent; do not promote 229CV to the primary J theorem without a true occupied-value bound.

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CU — three-color balanced 2/4-valuation scalar and fixed-value fibers
STATUS: POST_229CT_BALANCED_THREE_COLOR_SCALAR / EXACT_2_4_VALUATION_FINGERPRINT / UNITARY_FULL_BALANCED_MARK / HEIGHT_B3_FIXED_VALUE_B_O / G0_MARKED_HEIGHT_B5 / NO_GLOBAL_COUNT / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN
CARD_DOC_ID=1mBm3WHGbX7fJQagCJfy50HDtXd1w1MCj6tzo3Klh840
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA=Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CT
OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY=M3-T11-229; LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION=M3-T11-228; M3-T11-230 NOT_ISSUED.
PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN; GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0; P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false; PRODUCTION HOLD.


1. Scope and retained facts


All statements concern the exact positive primitive Stage37 S_B^hard13(delta) physical source, R<=B, all retained simultaneous selectors. Work only in the balanced B-state of 229CP/229CQ.


Write A=R-U, Bv=R-V, C=R-z, S=A+Bv+C<R, s=A+Bv, t=A+C, u=Bv+C, H_A=st, H_B=su, H_C=tu. Retain the three pairwise-coprime positive balanced blocks D_U=k_U^2, D_V=k_V^2, D_z=k_z^2, with
D_U || A,u,S; D_V || Bv,t,S; D_z || C,s,S.
The full balanced block is L_B=D_U D_V D_z=(k_U k_V k_z)^2 || S.
Set K_B=k_U k_V k_z and J_B=rad(K_B)=rad(k_U)rad(k_V)rad(k_z).
The 229CS orientation marks are M_A=k_Vk_z, M_B=k_Uk_z, M_C=k_Uk_V and M_i^2 || H_i. Each fixed H_i has uniformly B^o(1) physical endpoints by retained 229BY Sections 2-4. DO NOT use 229BY retracted Section 5 radical triangle (229BZ correction).
The canonical orientation i_*(P) maximizes rad(M_i) in tie order A<B<C, so J_B>K gives rad(M_bal)>K^(2/3). Retain gcd(G0,J_B)=1 from 229CH, G0=gcd(eR,xy), sf(G0)>T=B^(1/3-delta) on the current source.


2. Full three-color 2/4 valuations in one scalar


Define for i in {A,B,C}
W_i := S H_i,
F_i := K_B^2 M_i^2 = k_omit(i)^2 M_i^4,
where k_omit(A)=k_U, k_omit(B)=k_V, k_omit(C)=k_z.


Prove that F_i || W_i, not merely F_i | W_i.


For orientation A, a U-color balanced prime p divides A but neither Bv nor C (the prime-exclusion argument already used in 229CS). Mod p, s=A+Bv reduces to Bv and t=A+C reduces to C; hence p does not divide H_A=st. For V and z colors, 229CS gives exactly the full valuations v_p(H_A)=v_p(D_V D_z) (the unitary statement M_A^2 || H_A). Meanwhile L_B || S supplies v_p(S)=v_p(D_U D_V D_z) for all three balanced colors. Therefore for p|K_B:
- if p|k_U, v_p(W_A)=2 v_p(k_U);
- if p|k_V k_z, v_p(W_A)=4 v_p(k_V k_z).
There are no other balanced prime factors in W_A. Thus
F_A=k_U^2(k_Vk_z)^4 || W_A.
The B and C orientations are cyclic:
F_B=k_V^2(k_Uk_z)^4 || W_B,
F_C=k_z^2(k_Uk_V)^4 || W_C.
In every orientation, rad(F_i)=J_B and M_i^4 || W_i. The 2/4 exponents are the ACTUAL full p-adic valuations of W_i at the balanced primes, not an independently chargeable fourth-power divisibility density.


RESULT_229CU_THREE_COLOR_EXACT_UNITARY_2_4_VALUATION_FINGERPRINT=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229CU_FULL_BALANCED_RADICAL_IS_MARKED_IN_ONE_SH_SCALAR=PROVED_EXACT.


3. Canonical height-B^3 scalar and physical fixed-value fiber


Define W_bal:=S H_bal and F_bal:=K_B^2 M_bal^2. Since 0<S<R<=B and 0<H_bal<S^2<R^2, 
0<W_bal<B^3, F_bal || W_bal, rad(F_bal)=J_B.


For any fixed w, each physical endpoint with W_bal=w induces a positive divisor S|w and H_bal=w/S. There are at most tau(w) divisors; for each fixed H_bal, the endpoint set lies in the union of the three retained fixed-H_i fibers, each B^o(1). Since w<B^3, tau(w)=B^o(1). Hence uniformly
#{P:R<=B, W_bal(P)=w}=B^o(1).
Fixing (w,F_bal), or adding either mark, can only reduce that fiber.

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CT — exact norm-S gcd triangle and full-J K^(2/3) marked-gcd compression
STATUS: POST_229CS_FULL_J_NORM_S_GCD_CROSSWALK / EXACT_LAMBDA_PAIR_RECOVERY / THREE_GCD_TRIANGLE / FULL_J_K_TWO_THIRDS_CANONICAL_MARK / BALANCED_MARK_IS_EXACT_B_STATE_COMPONENT / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN

1. Scope


Work on the exact current S_B^hard13(delta) positive primitive Stage37 source, R<=B.

Bv=R-V,
C=R-z,

H_A=s t=A^2+2d^2,
H_B=s u=Bv^2+2d^2,
H_C=t u=C^2+2d^2,                                           (CT.1)


with
0<H_A,H_B,H_C<S^2<R^2<=B^2
and uniform B^o(1) fixed-value physical fibers.


Retain 229CF/229CO


lambda_U=gcd(A,S),
lambda_V=gcd(Bv,S),
lambda_z=gcd(C,S),                                           (CT.2)


the lambda_i pairwise coprime odd integers, and


L_J=lambda_U lambda_V lambda_z,
J=rad_odd(L_J).                                              (CT.3)


Retain the 229CP four-state decomposition and the 229CS balanced marks
M_A^2=D_VD_z,
M_B^2=D_UD_z,
M_C^2=D_UD_V.


2. Exact norm-S gcd crosswalk


Because
H_A=(S-C)(S-Bv),


we have
H_A == Bv*C mod S.                                           (CT.4A)


Hence


gcd(H_A,S)=gcd(Bv*C,S).                                      (CT.5A)


Now gcd(Bv,S)=lambda_V and gcd(C,S)=lambda_z.
The two gcds are coprime by the retained pairwise-coprimality of the lambda colors.
Therefore, prime-power by prime-power,


gcd(Bv*C,S)=lambda_V lambda_z.                               (CT.6A)


Thus exactly


C_A:=gcd(H_A,S)=lambda_V lambda_z.                           (CT.7A)


Cyclically,


C_B:=gcd(H_B,S)=lambda_U lambda_z,                           (CT.7B)
C_C:=gcd(H_C,S)=lambda_U lambda_V.                           (CT.7C)


RESULT_229CT_NORM_S_GCDS_RECOVER_THE_EXACT_TWO_COLOR_FULL_LAMBDA_BLOCKS=PROVED_EXACT.


This identity is full-valuation and is not restricted to the balanced B-state.


3. Exact three-gcd triangle


Since the lambda colors are pairwise coprime,


gcd(C_A,C_B)=lambda_z,                                       (CT.8A)
gcd(C_A,C_C)=lambda_V,                                       (CT.8B)
gcd(C_B,C_C)=lambda_U.                                       (CT.8C)


Also


gcd(C_A,C_B,C_C)=1,                                         (CT.9)
lcm(C_A,C_B,C_C)=L_J,                                       (CT.10)
C_A C_B C_C=L_J^2.                                          (CT.11)


Taking odd radicals,


rad(C_A) rad(C_B) rad(C_C)=J^2.                              (CT.12)


RESULT_229CT_THREE_NORM_S_GCDS_FORM_AN_EXACT_PAIRWISE_GCD_TRIANGLE=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229CT_PRODUCT_OF_THREE_NORM_S_GCDS_EQUALS_LJ_SQUARED=PROVED_EXACT.


Thus the full lambda triple can be recovered from the three low-height norm-S gcd receivers, without returning to the three outer gaps separately.


4. Full-J K^(2/3) canonical marked-gcd compression


From (CT.12),


max(rad(C_A),rad(C_B),rad(C_C)) >= J^(2/3).                  (CT.13)


Therefore for every K>=1,


J>K
implies that at least one orientation i in {A,B,C} satisfies


rad(C_i)>K^(2/3),
C_i=gcd(H_i,S),
C_i<=S<B.                                                     (CT.14)


Choose a deterministic maximizing orientation i_J with tie order A<B<C and define


H_J:=H_{i_J},
C_J:=C_{i_J}.                                                (CT.15)


Then on J>K,


rad(C_J)>K^(2/3),                                            (CT.16)
C_J|H_J,
C_J|S,
C_J<=S<B,
H_J<B^2.                                                     (CT.17)


For each fixed marked pair (h,c),


{P:(H_J,C_J)=(h,c)}
is contained in the union of the three fixed-H_i fibers.
Therefore uniformly


#{P:R<=B,(H_J,C_J)=(h,c)}=B^o(1).                            (CT.18)


RESULT_229CT_FULL_J_LARGE_HAS_CANONICAL_NORM_S_GCD_ORIENTATION_AT_K_TWO_THIRDS=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229CT_CANONICAL_FULL_J_MARKED_NORM_GCD_HAS_B_O_FIXED_PAIR_FIBER=PROVED.


This K^(2/3) compression now applies to the full J branch, not only to the balanced B-state.


5. Balanced 229CS mark is exactly the B-state component of the low-height gcd


Work in the A orientation.
By 229CS,


M_A^2=D_VD_z,


where D_V and D_z are the full balanced B-state prime-power subblocks of lambda_V and lambda_z.


Since
C_A=lambda_V lambda_z,


the B-state component of C_A is exactly


(C_A)_B=D_VD_z=M_A^2.                                       (CT.19A)


Likewise


(C_B)_B=M_B^2,                                               (CT.19B)
(C_C)_B=M_C^2.                                               (CT.19C)


The B-state supports are disjoint from the R/P/S supports, so each is a unitary component:


M_A^2 || C_A,
M_B^2 || C_B,
M_C^2 || C_C.                                                (CT.20)


RESULT_229CT_229CS_BALANCED_SQUARE_MARK_IS_EXACTLY_THE_B_STATE_COMPONENT_OF_THE_NORM_S_GCD=PROVED_EXACT.


Thus 229CS is not a separate receiver species: it is the balanced square submark inside the new low-height full-J gcd triangle.


In particular, on a balanced-dominant orientation the same mark satisfies simultaneously


M_i^2 || C_i,
M_i^2 || H_i,
M_i^2 || S.                                                  (CT.21)


6. Desaturated quotient triangle


Define


N_A:=H_A/C_A,
N_B:=H_B/C_B,
N_C:=H_C/C_C.                                                (CT.22)


Since C_i is the full gcd with S,


gcd(N_A,S/C_A)=1,
gcd(N_B,S/C_B)=1,
gcd(N_C,S/C_C)=1.                                            (CT.23)


Also


H_A H_B H_C=(s t u)^2=Pi^2,                                 (CT.24)


while (CT.11) gives C_A C_B C_C=L_J^2.
Therefore


N_A N_B N_C=(Pi/L_J)^2.                                     (CT.25)


RESULT_229CT_DESATURATED_THREE_NORM_QUOTIENT_PRODUCT_IS_AN_EXACT_SQUARE=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229CT_EACH_DESATURATED_NORM_QUOTIENT_IS_COPRIME_TO_ITS_S_QUOTIENT=PROVED_EXACT.


Firewall:
(CT.25) is only an exact square-product identity. Do NOT infer a three-atom radical triangle from it. The 229BZ correction of the old 229BY Section 5 radical inference remains fully in force.


7. One-scalar marked companion


Define


Z_J:=H_J C_J.                                                (CT.26)


Then


0<Z_J<B^3.                                                   (CT.27)


For fixed z, there are only tau(z)=B^o(1) possible divisor choices h=H_J with c=z/h.
For each fixed h, the retained 229BY fixed-H fibers are B^o(1).
Hence


#{P:R<=B,Z_J(P)=z}=B^o(1).                                   (CT.28)


Moreover C_J|H_J, so


C_J^2 | Z_J,                                                 (CT.29)


and J>K implies


rad(C_J)>K^(2/3).                                            (CT.30)


RESULT_229CT_CANONICAL_FULL_J_GCD_PRODUCT_SCALAR_HAS_B3_HEIGHT_B_O_FIXED_FIBER_AND_LARGE_SQUARE_DIVISOR=PROVED.


This scalar is only a compact pushforward. Its large square divisor is not assigned an independent density.


8. Quantitative status and method firewall


No one-third endpoint count is proved here.


The new gain is exact theorem routing:

- the full lambda triple is recoverable from their pairwise gcds;
- J>K gives one canonical marked gcd C_J<B with radical >K^(2/3);
- the 229CS balanced square mark is the exact B-state component of that same gcd.


Do not:
- infer fixed-power sparsity from C_J<B and rad(C_J)>K^(2/3) alone;
- infer sparsity from the scalar lower bound Z_J>C_J^2;
- treat C_J|H_J and C_J|S as independent divisibility probabilities;
- use the square-product quotient identity (CT.25) to revive the retracted 229BY radical-triangle claim;
- discard the CP four-state labels when a proof needs to distinguish R/P/B/S excess behavior.


A quantitative closure still requires an occupied-image theorem for the realized marked pairs (H_J,C_J), or a state-aware refinement:

- R-state: retain 229CN rho lift;

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CS — three-orientation norm-square carrier and K^(2/3) balanced compression
STATUS: POST_229CR_THREE_NORM_ORIENTATION_BALANCED_COMPRESSION / BALANCED_PAIR_BLOCKS_ARE_UNITARY_SQUARES_IN_HA_HB_HC / K_TWO_THIRDS_PAIR_RADICAL_PIGEONHOLE / CANONICAL_MARKED_NORM_RECEIVER_B_O_FIXED_FIBER / LOW_HEIGHT_HBAL_AND_MARKED_G0_PRODUCTS / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN
CARD_DOC_ID=1Jc_c8AjL1h4EUH1UqVs9SlqzTjb8avat2-keBPaSXDI
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA=Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CR
OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY=M3-T11-229; LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION=M3-T11-228; M3-T11-230 NOT_ISSUED.
PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN; GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0; P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false; PRODUCTION HOLD.


1. Scope


Work on the exact current S_B^hard13(delta) positive primitive Stage37 source, R<=B.


Retain 229CQ/229CR balanced color blocks


L_B=D_U D_V D_z,
D_U=k_U^2,
D_V=k_V^2,
D_z=k_z^2,


with D_U,D_V,D_z pairwise coprime and


D_U||A,u,S,
D_V||Bv,t,S,
D_z||C,s,S,


where


A=R-U,
Bv=R-V,
C=R-z,


s=A+Bv,
t=A+C,
u=Bv+C,
S=A+Bv+C.


Retain


r_U=rad(k_U),
r_V=rad(k_V),
r_z=rad(k_z),


so


J_B=r_U r_V r_z.                                             (CS.1)


Retain 229BY's three norm receivers


H_A:=s t=A^2+2d^2,
H_B:=s u=Bv^2+2d^2,
H_C:=t u=C^2+2d^2.                                           (CS.2)


The fixed-value physical fibers of each H_A,H_B,H_C are uniformly B^o(1). The retraction in 229BZ affects only the old radical-triangle inference, not these fixed-value norm fibers.


2. Balanced pair blocks are exact unitary square divisors of the norm receivers


Define


M_A:=k_V k_z,
M_B:=k_U k_z,
M_C:=k_U k_V.                                                 (CS.3)


Because the three k_i are pairwise coprime,


rad(M_A)=r_V r_z,
rad(M_B)=r_U r_z,
rad(M_C)=r_U r_V.                                             (CS.4)


We prove the A orientation; the others are cyclic.


229CQ gives
D_z||s
and
D_V||t.


A z-color balanced prime divides C and s, but does not divide A or Bv individually; hence it does not divide
t=A+C.
Therefore the full z block D_z enters H_A=s t only through s.


Similarly a V-color balanced prime divides Bv and t but does not divide A or C, hence it does not divide
s=A+Bv.
Therefore D_V enters H_A only through t.


Since D_z and D_V are coprime,


D_V D_z=M_A^2 || H_A.                                        (CS.5A)


Cyclically,


M_B^2=D_U D_z || H_B,                                        (CS.5B)
M_C^2=D_U D_V || H_C.                                        (CS.5C)


RESULT_229CS_BALANCED_PAIR_BLOCKS_ARE_UNITARY_SQUARE_DIVISORS_OF_THREE_NORM_RECEIVERS=PROVED_EXACT.


This is not an independent divisibility density. The same balanced color blocks have simply been re-expressed on the already-retained physical norm receivers H_A,H_B,H_C.


3. Three-orientation K^(2/3) compression


Multiplying the three pair radicals gives


rad(M_A) rad(M_B) rad(M_C)
 =(r_Vr_z)(r_Ur_z)(r_Ur_V)
 =(r_Ur_Vr_z)^2
 =J_B^2.                                                      (CS.6)


Therefore


max(rad(M_A),rad(M_B),rad(M_C))
 >= J_B^(2/3).                                                (CS.7)


Hence for every K>=1,


J_B>K


implies that at least one orientation i in {A,B,C} satisfies


rad(M_i)>K^(2/3),
M_i^2||H_i.                                                   (CS.8)


RESULT_229CS_BALANCED_J_LARGE_HAS_THREE_NORM_ORIENTATION_COVER_AT_K_TWO_THIRDS=PROVED_EXACT.


This strictly improves the balanced internal pigeonhole exponent from the two-orientation K^(1/2) statement in 229CR to K^(2/3).


Precision:
this is a stronger balanced-coordinate compression, not a proof of a new global one-third exponent and not an automatic improvement of the 229CH occupied-tail theorem status.


4. Canonical marked norm receiver


Choose a deterministic orientation i_*(P) in {A,B,C} maximizing rad(M_i), with the fixed tie order A<B<C.


Define


H_bal:=H_{i_*},
M_bal:=M_{i_*}.                                               (CS.9)


Then exactly


M_bal^2 || H_bal,                                             (CS.10)


and if J_B>K,


rad(M_bal)>K^(2/3).                                           (CS.11)


Also


0<H_bal<S^2<R^2<=B^2,                                        (CS.12)


because each of s,t,u is positive and strictly less than S.


For any fixed positive h,


{P:H_bal(P)=h}
 is contained in
{H_A=h} union {H_B=h} union {H_C=h}.


229BY therefore gives uniformly


#{P:R<=B,H_bal(P)=h}=B^o(1).                                 (CS.13)


For fixed h, the number of possible unitary square marks M_bal^2||h is at most


2^omega(h)=B^o(1).                                            (CS.14)


Thus


#{P:R<=B,(H_bal,M_bal)=(h,m)}=B^o(1)                         (CS.15)


uniformly for realized marked pairs.


RESULT_229CS_CANONICAL_BALANCED_MARKED_NORM_RECEIVER_HAS_B_O_FIXED_FIBER=PROVED.


This replaces the balanced theorem-facing coordinate
(G0,Kx,M_x)/(G0,Ky,M_y)
by a single canonical norm value H_bal plus one unitary square mark, while preserving only subpower local branching.


5. Low-height scalar consequences


On the balanced J_B>K branch,


H_bal >= M_bal^2
       >= rad(M_bal)^2
       > K^(4/3).                                             (CS.16)


Define


Phi_bal:=G0 H_bal.                                            (CS.17)


Since G0<=B^2 and H_bal<B^2,


Phi_bal<B^4.                                                  (CS.18)


For fixed phi, there are at most tau(phi)=B^o(1) divisor choices for a candidate G0, then H_bal=phi/G0 is fixed. By (CS.13),


#{P:R<=B,Phi_bal(P)=phi}=B^o(1).                             (CS.19)


On the current source sf(G0)>T, hence G0>T. Therefore


J_B>K
implies
Phi_bal>T K^(4/3).                                            (CS.20)


At the current six-bucket balanced threshold K=T^(1/5),


Phi_bal>T^(19/15).                                            (CS.21)


RESULT_229CS_G0_TIMES_CANONICAL_NORM_HAS_B4_HEIGHT_B_O_FIXED_FIBER_AND_T_K_4_OVER3_LOWER_BOUND=PROVED.


This scalar does not preserve sf(G0) exactly; the G0 divisor marking is only B^o but remains logically necessary if a theorem needs the original squarefree-kernel condition.


6. Squareclass-preserving companion


Define


Xi_bal:=G0 H_bal^2.                                           (CS.22)


Then


sf(Xi_bal)=sf(G0),                                            (CS.23)


because H_bal^2 is an exact square.


Also


Xi_bal<B^6.                                                   (CS.24)


For fixed xi, there are B^o(1) divisor choices G|xi such that xi/G is a square; for each such G the positive H_bal is uniquely sqrt(xi/G), and (CS.13) gives B^o physical preimages. Hence


#{P:R<=B,Xi_bal(P)=xi}=B^o(1).                               (CS.25)


Balanced largeness gives


J_B>K
implies
Xi_bal>T K^(8/3).                                             (CS.26)


At K=T^(1/5),


Xi_bal>T^(23/15).                                             (CS.27)


RESULT_229CS_SQUARECLASS_PRESERVING_BALANCED_NORM_SCALAR_HAS_B6_HEIGHT_B_O_FIXED_FIBER=PROVED.
RESULT_229CS_BALANCED_J_LARGE_FORCES_SQUARECLASS_SCALAR_ABOVE_T_K_8_OVER3=PROVED_EXACT.


Again, a lower bound on a scalar value is not an occupied-value count.


7. Exact unitary fourth-power mark in the squareclass scalar


Because M_bal^2||H_bal and every balanced J prime is coprime to G0 by the retained 229CH gcd(J_sharp,G0)=1,


gcd(M_bal,G0)=1.                                              (CS.28)


Write


H_bal=M_bal^2 N,
gcd(M_bal,N)=1.                                               (CS.29)


Then


Xi_bal=G0 M_bal^4 N^2,


and therefore


M_bal^4 || Xi_bal.                                            (CS.30)


Thus on J_B>K, the squareclass-preserving one-scalar receiver Xi_bal has simultaneously


sf(Xi_bal)>T,
a unitary fourth-power divisor M_bal^4,
rad(M_bal)>K^(2/3).                                           (CS.31)


RESULT_229CS_BALANCED_MARK_BECOMES_A_LARGE_UNITARY_FOURTH_POWER_BLOCK_IN_XI_BAL=PROVED_EXACT.


This is an exact one-scalar reformulation of the balanced mark, not an independent fourth-power sieve.


8. Unrestricted norm-square summation remains quantitatively too weak


The new K^(2/3) orientation threshold does not by itself close the count.


Fix an orientation and a squarefree r=rad(M)>Y.
Since H_i<B^2 and M^2|H_i, M<B.
For fixed r, the retained prescribed-prime-support lemma gives only B^o(1) possible M of polynomial height supported on r.
For each M, the number of positive H_i<B^2 divisible by M^2 is at most B^2/M^2.
Each fixed H_i has B^o physical fiber.


Hence


#{P: some orientation has rad(M_i)>Y}
 << B^(2+o(1)) sum_{r>Y} r^(-2)
 << B^(2+o(1))/Y.                                             (CS.32)


With Y=K^(2/3),


N_B(B;K)
 << B^(2+o(1)) K^(-2/3).                                     (CS.33)


This is still far above B^(1/3) throughout the nonempty balanced range K<B^(1/2).
At the current K=T^(1/5), it is much too weak.


RESULT_229CS_UNRESTRICTED_THREE_NORM_SQUARE_DIVISOR_SUMMATION_IS_QUANTITATIVELY_TOO_WEAK=PROVED_METHOD_CEILING.


Thus do not replace the selector-aware occupied-value problem by unrestricted integer multiples of M^2.


9. Updated balanced theorem interface


The preferred balanced target is now

(H_bal,M_bal),


on the exact hard13 source, with

This is preferred over the 229CR two-orientation (G0,Kx,M_x)/(G0,Ky,M_y) coordinate for first attack because:

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CR — balanced square-root unitary cross-selector bridge and two-orientation residual-core compression
STATUS: POST_229CQ_BALANCED_SQRT_UNITARY_CORE_BRIDGE / OUTER_EUCLID_ROOT_AND_RESIDUAL_CORE_COMMON_FULL_BLOCK / TWO_ORIENTATION_KX_KY_SQRT_THRESHOLD / MARKED_UNITARY_DIVISOR_SUBPOWER_ENTROPY / NO_NEW_GLOBAL_COUNT / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN

PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN; GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0; P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false; PRODUCTION HOLD.


1. Scope


Work on the exact current S_B^hard13(delta) positive primitive Stage37 source, R<=B.


Retain 229CQ:
L_B=D_U D_V D_z,
where D_U,D_V,D_z are pairwise-coprime perfect squares, and


D_U||A,u,S,
D_V||Bv,t,S,
D_z||C,s,S,


with
A=R-U,
Bv=R-V,
C=R-z,
u=Bv+C,
t=A+C,
s=A+Bv,
S=A+Bv+C.


Put


k_U:=sqrt(D_U),
k_V:=sqrt(D_V),
k_z:=sqrt(D_z),                                               (CR.1)


and


r_U:=rad(k_U)=rad(D_U),
r_V:=rad(k_V)=rad(D_V),
r_z:=rad(k_z)=rad(D_z).


Thus


J_B=r_U r_V r_z.                                              (CR.2)


Retain the 229BN residual cores


E=g/h_edge,
X=c/c21,
Y=f/c12,


with E,X,Y pairwise coprime, and 229BO


Kx:=E X,
Ky:=E Y.                                                       (CR.3)


2. Balanced square roots are full unitary blocks of the residual cores


Take p^a||D_U.
Because D_U is a balanced saturated U-color block, 229CO/229CP give


a=v_p(A)=2v_p(Y).                                             (CR.4)


Since a is even,


v_p(k_U)=a/2=v_p(Y).                                          (CR.5)


No prime of k_U appears in Y/k_U. Therefore


k_U || Y.                                                      (CR.6)


Cyclically,


k_V || X,
k_z || E.                                                      (CR.7)


Because E,X,Y are pairwise coprime, k_U,k_V,k_z are pairwise coprime and


K_B:=k_U k_V k_z || E X Y.                                   (CR.8)


Moreover


rad(K_B)=J_B,
K_B^2=L_B||S.                                                  (CR.9)


RESULT_229CR_BALANCED_SQUARE_ROOTS_ARE_FULL_UNITARY_RESIDUAL_CORE_BLOCKS=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229CR_BALANCED_TOTAL_SQRT_BLOCK_IS_UNITARY_IN_EXY_RESIDUAL_PRODUCT=PROVED_EXACT.


Precision:
this is stronger than the earlier divisibility W_outer|EXY. It identifies the exact p-adic exponent of every balanced prime inside its residual core and proves unitary, not merely ordinary, divisibility.


3. Same full block occurs in the outer-gap Euclid root


For the physical Pythagorean triples
(U,y,R),
(V,x,R),
(z,e,R)
with contents c12,c21,h_edge, respectively, the standard primitive gap factorization gives integers q_U,q_V,q_z such that


odd(A/c12)=q_U^2,
odd(Bv/c21)=q_V^2,
odd(C/h_edge)=q_z^2.                                          (CR.10)


Equivalently this is the retained Euclid-root squareclass form of the three outer gaps; the 2-adic orientation is harmless because every balanced prime is >3.


For p^a||D_U, p is excluded from 2c12 and a=v_p(A). Hence


v_p(q_U)=a/2=v_p(k_U)=v_p(Y).                                 (CR.11)


Therefore


k_U || q_U
and
k_U || gcd(q_U,Y).                                            (CR.12)


Cyclically,


k_V || gcd(q_V,X),
k_z || gcd(q_z,E).                                            (CR.13)


RESULT_229CR_BALANCED_SQRT_BLOCK_IS_A_COMMON_UNITARY_BLOCK_OF_OUTER_EUCLID_ROOT_AND_NESTED_RESIDUAL_CORE=PROVED_EXACT.


This is the desired selector-aware bridge:
a balanced prime is not merely a large lambda modulus. Its square root is the same full p-adic block in two different Pythagorean selector systems.


4. Two-orientation residual-core compression


By (CR.6)-(CR.8),


M_x:=k_V k_z || Kx=EX,
M_y:=k_U k_z || Ky=EY.                                       (CR.14)


Their radicals are


rad(M_x)=r_V r_z,
rad(M_y)=r_U r_z.                                             (CR.15)


Since r_U,r_V,r_z are positive and pairwise coprime,


max(r_V r_z,r_U r_z)^2
 >= (r_V r_z)(r_U r_z)
 = J_B r_z
 >= J_B.                                                       (CR.16)


Hence


J_B>K
implies
max(rad(M_x),rad(M_y))>K^(1/2).                              (CR.17)


Since M_x||Kx and M_y||Ky,


J_B>K
implies
rad(Kx)>K^(1/2)
or
rad(Ky)>K^(1/2).                                              (CR.18)


RESULT_229CR_BALANCED_J_LARGE_HAS_TWO_ORIENTATION_RESIDUAL_CORE_RADICAL_COVER_AT_SQRT_THRESHOLD=PROVED_EXACT.


This improves the internal balanced-color pigeonhole from the 229CQ K^(1/3) single-color threshold to a K^(1/2) two-orientation threshold.


It does not improve the already-retained global numerical T^(11/10) threshold of 229CH; it supplies a different, selector-aware arithmetic receiver carrying the exact balanced unitary blocks.


5. Marked unitary divisor has only subpower local entropy


For any fixed positive integer Kx, the number of unitary divisors M_x||Kx is exactly at most


2^omega(Kx)=B^o(1),                                           (CR.19)


uniformly because Kx has polynomial physical height.
The same holds for Ky.


229BO proved


#{P:R<=B,(G0(P),Kx(P))=(G,K)}=B^o(1),
#{P:R<=B,(G0(P),Ky(P))=(G,K)}=B^o(1).                        (CR.20)


Therefore marking the balanced unitary block does not introduce fixed-power branching:


#{P:R<=B,(G0,Kx,M_x)=(G,K,M)}=B^o(1),                        (CR.21)


and symmetrically for (G0,Ky,M_y).


RESULT_229CR_MARKING_BALANCED_UNITARY_DIVISOR_OVER_FIXED_G0_KX_OR_KY_COSTS_ONLY_SUBPOWER=PROVED.


Thus the balanced branch has a new theorem-facing occupied-support form:


BALANCED_MARKED_RESIDUAL_CORE_OCCUPANCY:


count the union of realized triples


(G0,Kx,M_x),
sf(G0)>T,
M_x||Kx,
rad(M_x)>K^(1/2),


and the symmetric y-orientation,
on the exact hard13 source.


A fixed realized marked triple has only B^o(1) physical preimages.


6. Complementary one-scalar max-orientation receiver


Retain 229BO


Theta_x=G0 Kx^2,
Theta_y=G0 Ky^2,


with
sf(Theta_x)=sf(Theta_y)=sf(G0)
and B^o(1) fixed-value physical fibers.


Define


Psi_max:=max(Theta_x,Theta_y)
       =G0 max(Kx,Ky)^2.                                      (CR.22)


Then


sf(Psi_max)=sf(G0).                                           (CR.23)


For fixed t,


{P:Psi_max=t}
is contained in
{P:Theta_x=t} union {P:Theta_y=t},


so


#{P:R<=B,Psi_max=t}=B^o(1).                                  (CR.24)


A uniform height bound sharper than the old B^6 individual coarse bound is available.
From


e=h_edge Eab<R,
x=d0 b c21 X<R,


we obtain


Theta_x
 < R^4 c12/(h_edge^2 d0^2 a b^3 c21)
 <= R^5.                                                       (CR.25)


Similarly


Theta_y<=R^5.                                                  (CR.26)


Therefore


0<Psi_max<=B^5.                                               (CR.27)


On the current source sf(G0)>T, hence G0>T.
If J_B>K, (CR.18) gives max(Kx,Ky)>K^(1/2), so


Psi_max > T K.                                                (CR.28)


At the balanced six-bucket cutoff K=T^(1/5),


Psi_max > T^(6/5).                                            (CR.29)


RESULT_229CR_MAX_ORIENTATION_SCALAR_HAS_B5_HEIGHT_EXACT_SF_G0_AND_SUBPOWER_FIXED_FIBER=PROVED.
RESULT_229CR_BALANCED_J_LARGE_FORCES_MAX_ORIENTATION_SCALAR_ABOVE_TK=PROVED_EXACT.


This is a structural scalar compression only.
A lower bound on a scalar value does not imply a sparse occupied-value set.


7. Relation to prior receivers


229CH:
already gives the global J-large two-quadratic receiver cover with threshold T sqrt(K).
229CR does not supersede that quantitative routing.


The new content of 229CR is different:
- exact balanced square-root unitary exponents in E,X,Y;
- simultaneous common-unitary occurrence in the outer Euclid roots;
- K^(1/2) two-orientation compression specifically inside the balanced B-state;
- B^o fixed fibers after marking the unitary divisor over the 229BO (G0,Kx)/(G0,Ky) coordinates.


229CQ:
its unrestricted root-line summation remains closed as too weak.
229CR does not reopen it.


229CI:
separate Sigma_xy and Sigma_R tail attacks remain quantitatively false.
The Kx/Ky marked receiver is a cross-selector coordinate compression, not an independent multiplication of the dual radical tails.


8. Quantitative status and firewall


No one-third endpoint count is proved.


Do not:
- claim CR.18 improves the already-known CH global threshold exponent;
- infer sparsity merely from rad(Kx)>K^(1/2) or rad(Ky)>K^(1/2);

records.content:
﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CQ — balanced sub-block square-modulus packing and quartic-radical tail ceiling
STATUS: POST_229CP_BALANCED_COLOR_SUBBLOCK_EXTRACTION / FULL_GCD_NOT_REQUIRED_FOR_SQUARE_MODULUS_PACKING / FIXED_BALANCED_RADICAL_r_MINUS4 / J_B_TAIL_IMPROVED_TO_K_MINUS1_BUT_STILL_TOO_WEAK / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN
CARD_DOC_ID=1bWTR74sPgqdoB0-a-Lg1peoN490TcbL-vbT3hltXvdY
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA=Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CP
OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY=M3-T11-229; LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION=M3-T11-228; M3-T11-230 NOT_ISSUED.
PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN; GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0; P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false; PRODUCTION HOLD.


1. Scope


Work on the exact current S_B^hard13(delta) positive primitive Stage37 physical source, R<=B.


Retain 229CP's balanced square block L_B. Because the three color supports lambda_U,lambda_V,lambda_z are pairwise coprime, L_B has a unique color factorization


L_B=D_U D_V D_z,                                              (CQ.1)


where D_U,D_V,D_z are pairwise coprime perfect squares, each D_i is the full balanced prime-power block inside the corresponding lambda_i, and


J_B=r_U r_V r_z,
r_i=rad(D_i).                                                  (CQ.2)


For U color, balanced means every p^a||D_U satisfies


v_p(A)=v_p(u)=v_p(S)=a,
u=Bv+C,
a even.                                                        (CQ.3)


Since the p-support of lambda_U is absent from Bv and C individually, the same p-block appears in Pi only through u and in Omega only through A. Thus


D_U||A,
D_U||u,
D_U||S.                                                       (CQ.4)


Cyclically


D_V||Bv,t,S,   t=A+C,
D_z||C,s,S,    s=A+Bv.                                       (CQ.5)


RESULT_229CQ_BALANCED_BLOCK_HAS_EXACT_COLOR_SQUARE_SUBBLOCK_FACTORIZATION=PROVED_EXACT.


Since L_B=D_UD_VD_z||S and D_i>=r_i^2,


J_B^2=(r_Ur_Vr_z)^2 | L_B | S < B.                           (CQ.6)


Hence


J_B < B^(1/2).                                                (CQ.7)


RESULT_229CQ_BALANCED_RADICAL_HAS_DETERMINISTIC_SQUARE_ROOT_HEIGHT_CEILING=PROVED_EXACT.


2. Sub-block square-modulus packing lemma


The key point is that 229CG's lattice packing does not require the chosen modulus to equal the full opposite gcd.


Fix a positive odd integer m and consider U-color endpoints satisfying


m|A,
m|u=Bv+C,
gcd(m,2d)=1.                                                  (CQ.8)


Put


Xopp=Bv-C.


The retained exact norm identity is


Xopp^2+8d^2=u(u+4A).                                         (CQ.9)


Therefore


m^2 | Xopp^2+8d^2.                                           (CQ.10)


Since 2d is invertible modulo m^2, define


sigma == Xopp*(2d)^(-1) mod m^2.


Then


sigma^2 == -2 mod m^2,
Xopp == 2sigma d mod m^2.                                    (CQ.11)


For any fixed m, the number of possible roots sigma modulo m^2 occurring on endpoints is at most


2^omega(m)=B^o(1).                                           (CQ.12)


For each root, (Xopp,d) lies in the rank-two lattice


Lambda(m,sigma)={(X,Y): X==2sigma Y mod m^2}


of determinant m^2.


Every nonzero lattice vector satisfies
m^2 | X^2+8Y^2,
so its weighted norm is at least m. The same ellipse/lattice packing argument as 229CG gives


#{(Xopp,d): |Xopp|<B,0<d<B}
 << 1+B^2/m^2.                                               (CQ.13)


For fixed (Xopp,d), put N=Xopp^2+8d^2.
From (CQ.9), u is a positive divisor of N and


A=(N/u-u)/4,
Bv=(u+Xopp)/2,
C=(u-Xopp)/2.                                                 (CQ.14)


There are tau(N)=B^o(1) divisor choices. Remaining integrality, positivity, chamber and physical selectors only delete candidates, and 229BU reconstructs at most one endpoint from a surviving labelled gap triple.


Therefore uniformly for every fixed m satisfying (CQ.8),


#{P:R<=B, m|A(P), m|u(P), gcd(m,2d(P))=1}
 << B^o(1)(1+B^2/m^2).                                      (CQ.15)


Cyclic versions hold for (Bv,t) and (C,s).


RESULT_229CQ_FIXED_OPPOSITE_GCD_SUBBLOCK_SQUARE_MODULUS_PACKING=PROVED.


This strictly generalizes the use of 229CG's packing mechanism: full-gcd equality m=lambda_i is sufficient but not necessary.


3. Apply the lemma to balanced color blocks


For a fixed U-balanced full block D_U, 229CP/229CG give gcd(D_U,2d)=1, so


#{P:R<=B, D_U^bal(P)=D_U}
 << B^o(1)(1+B^2/D_U^2).                                    (CQ.16)


The same holds cyclically.


Now fix the squarefree balanced color radical r=rad(D_U).
Because D_U is a perfect square,


D_U >= r^2.                                                   (CQ.17)


By the retained 229BQ polynomial-height prescribed-support lemma, for fixed r there are only B^o(1) possible D_U<=B supported on r.
Hence


#{P:R<=B, r_U^bal(P)=r}
 << B^o(1)(1+B^2/r^4).                                      (CQ.18)


Cyclically for r_V,r_z.


RESULT_229CQ_FIXED_BALANCED_COLOR_RADICAL_PACKING_HAS_QUARTIC_RADICAL_DENOMINATOR=PROVED.


This improves the generic fixed full-lambda-radical denominator r^-2 from 229CG to r^-4 on the balanced color channel.


4. Unrestricted large-J_B tail


If


J_B=r_U r_V r_z > K,                                        (CQ.19)


then one color satisfies


r_i > K^(1/3).                                                (CQ.20)


Also r_i<B^(1/2) by D_i>=r_i^2 and D_i|S<B.


Using (CQ.18) and a union bound over the three colors,


N_B(B;K):=#{P:R<=B,J_B(P)>K}


<< B^o(1) sum_{K^(1/3)<r<=B^(1/2)}
   (1+B^2/r^4).                                              (CQ.21)


The cardinality term is B^(1/2+o(1)).
Since


sum_{r>Y} r^(-4) << Y^(-3),


with Y=K^(1/3),


N_B(B;K)
 << B^(1/2+o(1)) + B^(2+o(1))/K.                             (CQ.22)


RESULT_229CQ_UNRESTRICTED_BALANCED_J_TAIL_BOUND_B_HALF_PLUS_B2_OVER_K=PROVED.


This is a genuine quantitative improvement over applying 229CG to the full lambda radical, whose corresponding unrestricted term was only B^(2+o(1))K^(-1/3).


5. Quantitative ceiling


The improvement is still nowhere near the one-third target on the nonempty balanced range.


By (CQ.7), J_B<B^(1/2), so the only nonempty polynomial thresholds satisfy K<B^(1/2).
For every such K,


B^2/K > B^(3/2).                                             (CQ.23)


Thus (CQ.22) cannot imply o(B^(1/3)) anywhere in the nonempty polynomial J_B range.


At the current balanced six-bucket threshold


K=T^(1/5),
T=B^(1/3-delta),


(CQ.22) gives only


N_B(B;K)
 << B^(1/2+o(1))
    +B^(29/15+delta/5+o(1)),                                 (CQ.24)


still vastly above B^(1/3).


RESULT_229CQ_BALANCED_SUBBLOCK_ROOT_LINE_TAIL_IS_QUANTITATIVELY_TOO_WEAK_FOR_ONE_THIRD=PROVED_METHOD_CEILING.


Precision:
this is a ceiling of the unrestricted sub-block square-modulus summation method. It is not a lower bound on the true physical endpoint population and not a no-go theorem for selector-aware balanced counting.


6. Consequence for the balanced hard core


229CQ closes one tempting retry:


do not re-run 229CG merely replacing the full lambda_i by the balanced square sub-block and then sum its moduli unrestrictedly.


That route improves r^-2 to r^-4 but still fails by a large power.


The balanced block remains potentially useful only when coupled to genuinely additional same-physical structure, e.g.


- 229CK colored square-gap budget;
- 229CI dual-radical pair;
- the exact common-unitary condition L_B||Pi,Omega,S;
- or a new occupied-value theorem on the balanced color sub-block image.


The preferred balanced contract is therefore sharpened to


J_BALANCED_SELECTOR_AWARE_SUBBLOCK_OCCUPANCY:

D_U||A,u,S,
D_V||Bv,t,S,

together with the physical selectors, rather than unrestricted root-line summation.

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CP — four-state common-gcd valuation split and silent balanced-square channel
STATUS: POST_229CO_FOUR_STATE_VALUATION_REFINEMENT / RESIDUAL_OMEGA_EXCESS / SATURATED_PI_EXCESS / SATURATED_S_EXCESS / SILENT_BALANCED_TRIPLE_UNITARY_SQUARE / COMBINED_PI_SQUARE_MODULUS / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN
